reason: The passage demonstrates that non-leaders also possess agency with consequential outcomes. Most significantly, an unnamed archer (אִישׁ מָשַׁךְ בַּקֶּשֶׁת לְתֻמּוֹ) draws his bow 'at random' and strikes down King Ahab, killing him and fundamentally altering the course of events. This ordinary soldier, described without any leadership title or position, exercises decisive agency independent of commands from leaders. While the narrative emphasizes the decisions and orders of various leaders (King Ahab, Jehoshaphat, the King of Aram, the prophets), the climactic action—the death of the king—is accomplished by a non-leader acting on his own initiative. This contradicts the assertion that only leaders possess agency.
